name: Contraction Avoidance Profiling
description: Measures the frequency of spelled-out auxiliary verbs versus their contracted forms (e.g., 'do not' vs. 'don't') to detect artificial formality.
mechanism: Large Language Models inherently default to a polite, formal, and authoritative tone, an artifact of their alignment training (e.g., RLHF) designed to prevent them from sounding overly colloquial or unprofessional. As a direct consequence, they exhibit a strong statistical bias toward morphological expansion—spelling out words fully ('cannot', 'do not', 'it is', 'they are') rather than using natural human contractions ('can't', 'don't', 'it's', 'they're'). Human writers, even in relatively professional contexts, naturally blend contractions into their writing to maintain rhythmic flow and conversational readability. This method computes the ratio of uncontracted verb/pronoun pairings to their contracted alternatives within a text. A severe deficit in contractions, especially in contexts intended to be casual, persuasive, or narrative, strongly correlates with synthetic generation.
useCase: Analyzing blogs, emails, marketing copy, and casual essays where an overly stiff, contraction-less tone betrays the presence of an AI generator attempting to sound authoritative.
strengths:
• Highly effective on 'conversational' or 'informal' prompts where the AI fails to drop its inherent formal alignment.
• Fast, deterministic, and computationally lightweight, relying on simple regex and lexical mapping.
• Difficult for basic AI generators to overcome without explicit, heavily engineered prompts instructing them to use contractions.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives on deeply formal human writing, such as academic dissertations, legal contracts, or official corporate press releases where contractions are forbidden.
• Completely inapplicable to languages that do not feature syntactical contractions (e.g., Chinese, Japanese, Korean), limiting this metric primarily to English and specific European languages.
• Easily bypassed by prompt engineers who explicitly add 'use plenty of contractions' or 'write casually' to their instructions.
parameters:
Analysis: Lexical Regex Matching & Morphological Ratio
Metric: Fully Expanded Forms vs. Available Contraction Opportunities
Output: 0-100 Formality Rigidity (Contraction Deficit) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-75%. Highly dependent on the expected genre of the text. Extremely useful as a secondary indicator alongside vocabulary rarity and sentence length variance.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
